info.name: Cyfuture DBaaS
info.description: DBaaS manages projects and databases. Immutable IDs (prj-xxxx, db-xxxx) identify resources; database names are human-facing handles. Omit a database name to receive a unique engine-prefixed handle. Keep an Idempotency-Key unchanged only when retrying the exact same request. The Backup and Restore folder supports manual full backups, scheduled backups, retention, PITR, and restores into new databases.

item.name: Projects

request.description: Only displayName and description are accepted. The backend assigns projectId and namespace internally. Omit displayName if you want a generated friendly name.

exec: pm.test('Project deletion returns a status', function () { pm.expect([200, 202]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Returns a status body immediately. DBaaS deletes project databases and removes the namespace after database cleanup is complete.

item.description: Create, list, update, get, and delete DBaaS projects. Projects are top-level resources; there is no organization selection or organization API.

item.name: Database Provisioning

request.description: Deploys POSTGRESQL in STANDALONE mode. Run Database Options first to verify the versions installed on the target cluster.
Deploys POSTGRESQL in REPLICATION mode with scheduled full-backup settings.
Deploys MYSQL in STANDALONE mode. Run Database Options first to verify the versions installed on the target cluster.
Deploys MYSQL in REPLICATION mode. Run Database Options first to verify the versions installed on the target cluster.
Deploys MONGODB in STANDALONE mode. Run Database Options first to verify the versions installed on the target cluster.
Deploys MONGODB in REPLICA_SET mode. Run Database Options first to verify the versions installed on the target cluster.
Deploys MONGODB in SHARDING mode. Run Database Options first to verify the versions installed on the target cluster.

item.description: Create examples for all engine/mode combinations supported by the backend. Backup configuration is required at creation; edit each backup object to choose the desired schedule, retention, timezone, and PITR setting. Name is optional: omitted names receive a unique engine-prefixed handle. Each successful request stores databaseId and operationId for the lifecycle requests below.

item.name: Scaling & Expansion

request.description: KubeBlocks first prefers an in-place resize. If that is unsupported, DBaaS allows a replication-safe pod recreation. Poll Get Operation: it succeeds only after ready pods report the requested CPU and memory, and InstanceUpdateRestricted is surfaced instead of leaving the operation RUNNING indefinitely.

item.description: Project-scoped KubeBlocks OpsRequest examples. Set databaseId to a RUNNING database first. Vertical scaling uses PreferInPlace and safely falls back to a replication-aware pod recreation when required. For MongoDB sharding use componentName values such as mongos, config-server or shard.

request.description: Restarts every component in the database. Do not send a request body.

Disable deletion protection before calling this endpoint. DBaaS keeps the database in DELETING until the KubeBlocks Cluster and all database-specific credential/helper resources are gone; shared services and KubeBlocks child resources are not manually deleted.

item.name: Backup and Restore
item.description: Configure scheduled backups, retention, PITR, independent restore points, and temporary private restores. Restores always create a new temporary private database, never overwrite the source, and must be promoted before expiry to become permanent. Keep each Idempotency-Key unchanged only when retrying the identical request; use a new key for a new operation.

request.description: Updates product-level schedule, retention, timezone, and PITR settings. Cron uses five fields.
Returns product-level scheduled-backup, retention, and PITR settings with current status and safe errors.

exec: pm.test('Recovery window response is available', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
const safe = new Date(start + Math.floor((end - start) / 2)).toISOString();

request.description: Returns observed PITR health and the startsAt/endsAt recovery bounds. Only use a point-in-time restore when status is READY.

exec: pm.test('Backup create response has expected status', function () { pm.expect([200, 202, 409, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });
if (pm.response.code === 409) { pm.test('Backup conflict is explicit', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.be.empty; }); }
if (pm.response.code === 422) { pm.test('Backup validation is explicit', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.be.empty; }); }

request.description: Creates a manual FULL backup. Set type to INCREMENTAL to create an incremental backup through this same endpoint; it requires a completed base backup. The response contains the backupId, type, status, timestamps, retention expiry, size, and safe errors. retentionDays is optional and must be 1-3650 when supplied.
Lists the database's full and incremental backup history with product-level status, timestamps, size, expiry, and safe errors.
Returns the current product-level backup status and history.
Lists full and point-in-time restore history for this source database. Each item identifies its newly created target database.

exec: pm.test('Restore response has expected status', function () { pm.expect([200, 202, 409, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Creates an independent temporary private restore database from a completed backup. This never overwrites the source database and never creates a permanent database until Promote Restore succeeds.

exec: pm.test('Restore response has expected status', function () { pm.expect([200, 202, 409, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Run Get PITR Recovery Window first. restoreTime is auto-set to a safe midpoint inside the window, not exactly at endsAt. The restore always targets a new temporary private database.
Returns the current restore status and the ID of the newly created target database.

exec: pm.test('Restore status response has expected status', function () { pm.expect([200, 409, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });
pm.test('Active restore response has expected status', function () { pm.expect([200, 409, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Returns the one active temporary restore for the source database, if present.

exec: pm.test('Promote response has expected status', function () { pm.expect([200, 409, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });
if (pm.response.code === 409) { pm.test('Promote conflict is explicit', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.be.empty; }); }

request.description: Promotes a READY temporary restored database. Promotion removes expiry and does not delete or modify the source database.

exec: pm.test('Delete temporary restore response has expected status', function () { pm.expect([200, 202, 409, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });
if (pm.response.code === 409) { pm.test('Delete conflict is explicit', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.be.empty; }); }

request.description: Deletes the temporary restored database only. The source database ID remains {{databaseId}} and is not targeted.

exec: pm.test('Restored connection response has expected status', function () { pm.expect([200, 409, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Returns credentials for the restored database. Do not print or share the complete connection URI in logs.
Deletes the known backup and its retained backup data. It is blocked while a restore from this backup is active.
